messages:
mia: Hey team — design review request. Putting up a quick Figma for the convo pane iteration: https://figma.com/file/xyz/playground-convo-pane — main asks: 1) stop/regenerate affordance placement (inline bubble vs global toolbar), 2) token counter visibility while streaming (should it collapse/compact?), 3) prompt library card interaction (pin vs flyout). Screenshot here: https://img.redwood.dev/shot.png

avi: taking a look. Can you drop the specific flows you want us to evaluate? quick accept/reject would help.

mia: Quick flows: A) inline stop button inside message bubble (top-right), B) global floating toolbar at bottom-left with stop + regen. For tokens: show compact count (e.g., "324 tok") while streaming, full expanded on hover. Prompt card: inline pin icon to keep in rail.

sam: my 2¢ — inline button feels more discoverable during streaming, less mouse travel for users watching output. But it makes message chrome heavier. Global toolbar cleaner for small screens.

kevin: a11y note: whichever you pick, ensure the stop control is keyboard reachable without having to focus the message content first. It must be a real button with aria-label and not just an icon-only div. Also make streaming text updates in an aria-live region, but avoid verbosity for screen readers.

alisa: QA: need ARIA tests and keyboard flows. Also regression: does inline stop overlap copy actions (copy msg)? We had one bug where toolbar obscured selection on narrow widths.

mia: good call. Sam, can you mock the small-screen stacking? I worry inline could push action menu off-screen on mobile.

sam: yep — quick CSS idea: position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; z-index: 2; for bubbles > collapsed width it moves into overflow menu. For mobile we can hide inline and show floating toolbar. Code snippet: 
```
.message-actions { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; display: flex; gap: 8px; }
@media (max-width: 640px) { .message-actions.inline { display: none; } .global-toolbar { display: flex; } }
```

kevin: copy suggestion for aria-labels: use "Stop generation" not just "Stop" — clearer for assistive tech. For the token counter present short aria-label like "Token usage: 324 tokens" and keep token updates polite (aria-live="polite").

avi: microcopy: on regen confirm, should we say "Regenerate response" or "Regenerate from prompt"? I lean toward the shorter one. Also want a tooltip for the compact token display: "Estimated tokens used so far"

mia: agreed on "Regenerate response". For token compactness: show short numeric while streaming; on hover expand to full label. On keyboard focus show expanded too.

sam: implementation detail — caching the token count per-session is cheaper than recalculating per-frame. We can emit token updates from the server every 250ms to keep the UI snappy but not thrash.

design-bot: automated preview posted — https://img.redwood.dev/preview_v2.png (option A inline stop / compact token)

kevin: accessibility checklist: 1) stop button reachable via Tab and Enter/Space, 2) aria-labels as above, 3) aria-live="polite" for streaming text, 4) token tooltip accessible via keyboard, 5) ensure color contrast for token badge meets AA.

alisa: test cases I need: keyboard-only regen + stop, token tooltip focus, mobile flow toolbar visible, selection not blocked when actions show. Also regression: VoiceOver reading each token update — ensure polite.

mia: votes? react with :one: for inline-by-default + bottom toolbar fallback on mobile, :two: for global toolbar only. Please add notes if you pick :two:.

sam: :one: — inline by default.

kevin: :one: — inline default, but hide on narrow widths.

avi: :one: but add product note: global toolbar as fallback for low-bandwidth streaming where inline might jitter.

alisa: :one: — adds tests to testplan ticket TICKET-451.

mia: sweet — decision: implement inline stop button (positioned top-right of bubble), fallback to global toolbar on <640px, token counter compact while streaming with hover/focus expand, prompt library pin icon to keep card in rail. Action items: sam to open PR with CSS + aria labels, kevin to PR a11y doc, alisa to add tests. I'll also update the figma with the mobile-stacked state. Targeting a small release next week. :thumbsup:

sam: will open branch: feature/playground-inline-stop and assign reviewers.

kevin: I'll draft quick a11y checklist in that PR comment.

alisa: I'll add testcases to the sprint board.

mia: thanks everyone — closing thread.
